title: y-constraints/0
description: The constraint file of a bare module, or of a library crate written by hand (proposal/bare-rust.md, 4.2 to 4.4, 7). Types are strings in the constraint language's type syntax, or host text.

crate.description: The crate and its version, as `name version`: `eve_cache 0.1.0`, or `std 1.97.0` for a library file (named `<crate>-<version>.constraints.json`).

module.description: The module's file, relative to the crate root; for a library file, the library's root module path (`std`).

status.description: The default status of the file's clauses: a status name, as `strip` writes it (`lifted`), or a status with its reason, `{ "assumed": "hand-written" }`, which is language 10.2's `assumed … because "hand-written"`.

failures.description: The failures the file's clauses name, as language 15's `failure NAME : user | runtime`: the name and its class, or `{ "class": …, "payload": { field: type } }` when the failure carries a payload that `fails NAME { field: e } when p` fills. A library file for Rust declares `panic`, the Rust host's runtime failure, with `message` and `location`.

holes.description: Per function or constant (by subject name), the types that fill holes no slot covers.

views.description: Views declared for the file: named pure projections of state a value holds beyond its value (language 15's `view(e)`), each bound to a host function. Usable in any clause of the file.

type.description: A type string (`u64 as 'usize'`, `ref<Entry>?`, `map<K, V> as 'std::collections::HashMap'`, `Chars<'a>`, `some std::iter::Iterator { Item = u8 }`, `any std::error::Error as 'std::boxed::Box'`), or host text for a type the language has no form for.

form.description: Why the type is host text: the form that has no counterpart.

from.description: The parameter a result borrows from.

lifetime.description: A lifetime that elision cannot express, as written.

for.description: On a `type`: the lifetime parameters the type borrows for, `hold : borrows for 'a`. Each is a lifetime of the subject's `generics`.

name.description: A type parameter, or a lifetime with its quote.

where.description: Bounds written in a where clause. The constraint is the conjunction of `bounds` and `where`.

for.description: The bounded type, when it is not a parameter of the subject.

fails.description: `Result<T, E>` gives type `T` and fails with `E`.

name.description: The subject's path. A `use` is named `<scope>::use <path as written>`, and is a subject only when it has a visibility (`pub use a::b;`). In a library file, the canonical public path (`std::collections::HashMap::get`, `std::primitive::str::chars`, `std::vec!`).

bounds.description: Supertraits of a trait, or the bounds of an associated type.

trait.description: The implemented trait with its arguments, when the bare header has only its name; for a trait method in a library file, the trait with its arguments, `std::convert::From<T>`.

self.description: The type an impl is for, when the bare header has only its name.

implements.description: The interfaces a `type` declares it implements (language 6.11): the interface with its arguments, the associated types the implementation fixes, and, when the implementation is a subject of the file, its name. A library file writes them; `strip` writes one for each `impl Trait for T` whose `T` is a type of the file.

assoc.description: For an `impl`: its associated types, `Item` to the type it is.

impl.description: For a function in a library file: the `impl` subject whose method it is. The function is checked as `<Self as Trait>::name`, with the impl's generics.

form.description: For a macro: how it is invoked. A `derive` macro is named like its trait with a `!`, `std::fmt::Debug!`.

clauses.description: What the signature slots cannot say, in order.

views.description: Views of this subject, as the file's `views` without `of`.

derive.description: For a type with `fields` or `variants`: the derive templates (`Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash`, `Default`, `Copy`) it uses, which `libfmt --expand` expands into one clause per field.

locals.description: `local name : T`, keyed by the binding's bare pattern text; `#2` marks a second `let` of the same pattern.

hints.description: Body hints, by kind and the ordinal of the site among sites of that kind in the body.

sep.description: A literal's suffix was written with an underscore: `1_u8`.

assumed.description: Taken on trust, because: `hand-written`, `documentation`, a person's name.

proven.description: What proved it: `rustc: signature compiled`, a Kani harness.

lifted.description: The code that enforces it: `std/src/vec/mod.rs: assert!(index <= len)`.

observed.description: What it was seen in: an analysis of the body, a run.

clause.description: A clause the signature slots cannot say. `kind` names the family and `text` is the clause in the syntax of language 15, keyword included (`ensure found : result == self[k]`); `panics` is `fails panic when p`, `panic` being the Rust host's runtime failure. A `callback` clause may name the call's arguments and result (`callback f : called exactly once when exists self, with self, returning r`; the names `with` gives and `returning` binds are in scope in the subject's other clauses, language 6.13), and a `protocol` is a regular expression over the subject's calls (`protocol self.next+`). `unexpressed` is a promise the language cannot state: `text` is free text and `reason` says why the language cannot say it. Those are the gaps that feed proposal 12.

given.description: Conditions the promise relies on (language 6.12): the clause holds whenever all of them hold, and says nothing otherwise. Each is `default` (the default body of a trait method is not overridden), `build SETTING` (a setting of the host profile: overflow_checks, debug_assertions, panic=unwind, panic=abort), or `P.m, P.n never panic | terminate | effects none` (the named methods of the bound implementations of the generic parameter `P`). The clause `text` stays the unconditional form; the language form is `text given item and item`. Allowed on never panics, effects, ensure, fails and panics clauses.

source.description: Where the clause comes from: a documentation section or a source location, with its version.

status.description: Overrides the file's status for this clause.

of.description: The subject the view reads, quoted: `'std::vec::Vec'`. Required in the file's list; a subject's own list means that subject.

host.description: The pure host function the view is bound to, quoted and under `of`: `'std::vec::Vec::capacity'`. A clause calls the view by name: `capacity(self)`.

assoc.description: The associated types this implementation fixes: `{ "Item": "char" }`.

impl.description: The name of the `impl` subject that carries this implementation's generics, `where` and clauses.
